title: Sam Altman said AI hasn't led to 4-hour workweeks because people are competitive
excerpt: The OpenAI CEO said that as people become more productive, they will also become more competitive and want to work more.
content_html:
Sam Altman said AI won't usher in the golden age of the four-hour workweek.

In an interview with host Ti Morse on his "Relentless" podcast, released on Saturday, the OpenAI CEO talked about why AI has not led to shorter workweeks for most people.

"Technology, for a long time, has been promising people that they're going to work less and they're going to have all this leisure," Altman said.

He said this trend has played out to some extent, with people having more time for leisure than at previous points in history and a higher quality of life.

"But somehow we never get the promise of the four-hour workweek at mass scale in society," he said. "And I don't expect AI to change that."

He said that as AI drives productivity gains, people are increasingly expecting more of themselves.

"We always want more. We think of new things to do, to create for each other, to want for ourselves. It's like a relative game. People are very focused on how they're doing relative to other people," Altman said.

He said that competition drives the economy and will not stop.

"I think we're all going to be much busier than we thought we were supposed to be in a post-superintelligence world. We're still going to complain about it, but secretly we're going to be happy," Altman said.

The idea of shorter, more flexible workweeks emerged post-pandemic as a way to address employee burnout and give workers greater control over their workdays.

In 2023, Business Insider spoke with small businesses that said transitioning to a four-day work model raised employee morale and boosted productivity.

With the C-suite doubling down on five-day return-to-office mandates and promoting the notorious 9-9-6 work culture — working from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week — the dream of a four-day workweek has slipped further out of reach.

In the same interview, Altman said AI is now in "the singularity," a point at which artificial intelligence surpasses human intelligence and may begin going rogue.

His comments followed OpenAI's latest models breaking out of their sandbox and hacking into a dataset from another AI company, Hugging Face.

Still, Altman said the singularity would be "incredible, hugely positive, awesome for the world."

content_html_zh:
萨姆·奥尔特曼表示，人工智能不会迎来每周工作四小时的黄金时代。

在周六发布的“Relentless”播客中接受主持人 Ti Morse 采访时，这位 OpenAI 首席执行官谈到了为什么人工智能没有让大多数人缩短每周的工作时间。

奥特曼说：“长期以来，技术一直向人们承诺，他们将减少工作量，并拥有所有这些闲暇。”

他表示，这种趋势已经在一定程度上发挥了作用，人们比历史上以前有更多的休闲时间，生活质量也更高。

“但不知何故，我们从未得到社会大规模每周工作四小时的承诺，”他说。 “我不认为人工智能会改变这一点。”

他表示，随着人工智能推动生产力的提高，人们对自己的期望越来越高。

“我们总是想要更多。 我们思考新的事情要做，为彼此创造，为自己想要。 这就像一场相对的游戏。 人们非常关注自己相对于其他人的表现，”奥特曼说。

他表示，竞争驱动经济，不会停止。

“我认为在后超级智能世界中，我们都会比我们想象的更加忙碌。 我们仍然会抱怨，但私下里我们会很高兴，”奥特曼说。

更短、更灵活的工作周的想法是在大流行后出现的，作为解决员工倦怠问题并让员工更好地控制自己工作日的一种方式。

2023 年，《商业内幕》与小型企业进行了交谈，他们表示，过渡到四天工作模式提高了员工士气并提高了生产力。

随着最高管理层加倍执行为期五天的重返办公室任务，并推广臭名昭著的 9-9-6 工作文化——从上午 9 点开始工作。 每周工作六天到晚上 9 点——每周工作四天的梦想已经变得更加遥不可及。

在同一次采访中，奥特曼表示，人工智能现在正处于“奇点”，在这个点上人工智能超越了人类智能，并可能开始变得失控。

在他发表评论之前，OpenAI 的最新模型突破了沙箱，并侵入了另一家人工智能公司 Hugging Face 的数据集。

尽管如此，奥特曼表示，奇点将是“令人难以置信的、非常积极的、对世界来说令人敬畏的”。
